policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the earth shook and trembled' does not distinguish the qere from the consonantally identical ketiv; no mapped textual-variant note decides the reading, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV 'discomfited them' explicitly renders the object 'them', distinguishing ketiv ויהמם from qere ויהם.
ASV 'all his ordinances were before me' uses the plural 'ordinances', distinguishing qere משפטיו from singular ketiv משפטו.
ASV's main text says 'in his way', distinguishing ketiv דרכו from qere דרכי ('my way'); the alternative_rendering note does not decide a textual reading.
ASV's main text says 'his feet', distinguishing ketiv רגליו from qere רגלי ('my feet'); the mapped textual_variant note identifies 'my' only as the other reading.
ASV's main text 'Great deliverance giveth he' renders the ketiv מגדיל; the mapped textual_variant note assigns 'He is a tower of deliverance' to the other reading.
